business_problem: STACKIT needed a sovereign cloud database foundation that could keep customer data under EU control, handle complex hierarchical workloads, and reliably support large-scale retail and managed-service operations without depending on third-party servers.
solution_summary: Schwarz Group built STACKIT as a secure cloud platform for internal subsidiaries and later external customers, then standardized database workloads on MongoDB to enforce data sovereignty and flexible document storage. The in-house developed database services run on Kubernetes within STACKIT's OpenStack-based infrastructure, where MongoDB stores complex hierarchies and serves workloads that range from managed customer services to Lidl's automated food-ordering calculations. Because the platform stays in Schwarz-controlled data centers in Germany and Austria, the team can offer EU data residency and visibility into who accesses data while still giving developers a familiar, high-performance document database. MongoDB also fits STACKIT's commercial model: it supports scalable managed services, helps the company package cloud offerings for regulated customers, and provides reliable overnight processing for retail logistics without separate dedicated hardware dependencies.

solution_components.name: MongoDB
solution_components.role: Provides the document database layer for STACKIT's sovereign cloud services and critical retail workloads.

data_flow: Managed-service workloads and retail inventory data flow into MongoDB running on STACKIT's Kubernetes-based cloud. For Lidl, nightly store-hour and inventory inputs are processed into stock requirements, and the resulting calculations feed logistics execution while remaining inside Schwarz-controlled infrastructure.
business_outcome: STACKIT turned sovereign data control into a customer-facing cloud offering, supported demanding retail calculations reliably, and gave regulated customers a scalable EU-resident alternative to hyperscaler-managed data services.
